home.name: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen
home.news: Still without Alex Lyon (upper body), the Sabres will keep leaning on Luukkonen, turning to him for the third time in four games. That said, Luukkonen's de facto starting netminder role hasn't translated into success. The 27-year-old Finnish goalie has allowed eight goals on 37 shots (.784 SV%) in two outings, but has salvaged a 1-1-0 record. The Sabres enter Thursday's contest as slight +105 home underdogs against a Dallas Stars team coming off a one-sided 5-0 victory over the San Jose Sharks.

home.name: Jacob Fowler
home.news: Samuel Montembeault's disastrous 2025-26 season, which led to a demotion to the AHL, thrust Fowler into some NHL action, but Montembeault started the 2026-27 season with the Canadiens, resulting in Fowler playing with Laval (AHL). That said, an early-season injury to Montembeault has given Fowler an NHL opportunity, and he will tend the twine for the first time this season on Thursday against the Nashville Predators. The 21-year-old Fowler played well last season in his NHL debut, posting a 2.43 GAA and .908 SV% in 17 games (9-6-2). The Canadiens enter Thursday's contest as -171 home favourites.

home.name: Pyotr Kochetkov
home.news: Hurricanes' Head Coach Rod Brind'Amour started Brandon Bussi in the first two games of the season, but he seems to be easing into an even goalie rotation, with Kochetkov tending the twine on Thursday in his second start of the season. The 27-year-old Kochetkov missed most of the 2025-26 season with a lower-body injury, but he played well in his return to action, saving 16 of 18 shots (.889 SV%) in a 3-2 win over the Philadelphia Flyers. The Hurricanes enter Thursday's contest as enormous -337 home favourites against the surprisingly potent early-season offense of the Vancouver Canucks, who have scored 19 goals in their first four games (2-2-0).

home.name: Ilya Sorokin
home.news: Sorokin had the night off in New York's previous game, but he will likely return to the crease on Thursday against the Chicago Blackhawks, looking to build on a strong start to the 2026-27 season. The 31-year-old goalie has been outstanding through two games, despite a 1-1-0 record, saving 61 of 63 combined shots (.968 SV%). Sorokin had the worst save percentage of his career in 2025-26 (.906 SV%) and hopes to improve those totals this season under new Head Coach Pete DeBoer.
